question: Which MUTCD table gives a fixed replacement interval, in years, for every type of traffic sign?
model_answer: Direct Answer: The evidence provided does not contain any MUTCD table that prescribes a fixed replacement interval, in years, for every type of traffic sign — and no such table appears to exist in the material supplied. The closest item in the evidence, Table 1B-1, lists target compliance dates for specific new MUTCD provisions (e.g., specific sign installation requirements and a pavement-marking retroreflectivity method), which is fundamentally different from a sign replacement schedule. None of the Standard provisions supplied addresses sign service life or replacement intervals. Visual evidence: - [Image 2] Table 1B-1, "Target Compliance Dates Established by the FHWA," lists compliance deadlines (e.g., January 18, 2029; September 6, 2026; January 18, 2034) for particular MUTCD provisions such as Weight Limit signs and Low Clearance signs — it is not a sign replacement-interval table. - [Image 3] Figure 1B-2 illustrates the process for incorporating new traffic control devices into the MUTCD and does not address sign replacement. - [Image 4] Figure 2L-1 concerns changeable message sign pixel pitch and legend display capability, not sign replacement intervals. - [Image 1] Figure 2G-18 shows regulatory signs for managed lanes and is unrelated to replacement schedules. - [Images 5–8] The full page views (Pages 23, 26, 104, 173) show tables of contents, sign figures, and retroreflectivity-related content, none of which establishes fixed replacement intervals by sign type. Citations: - Table 1B-1 (p.5) - Figure 1B-2 (p.10) - Figure 2L-1 (p.515) - Figure 2G-18 (p.435) In short: the evidence is insufficient to identify any such table, because the MUTCD material provided contains no table assigning fixed replacement intervals in years to all traffic sign types.
